rounds.text: Swastika Castal Ltd trades at a P/E of 20.6x [E1] and a lower P/E of 15.79x against a sector benchmark of 21.99x [E6], while offering an attractive EV/EBITDA of 9.99x compared to its sector benchmark of 12.26x [E11]. Fundamental profitability metrics are robust, featuring an ROCE of 19.6% [E12] and an ROE of 18.0% [E13], both outpacing the sector median ROCE of 13.5% [E53]. Growth momentum is exceptionally strong, driven by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 78% [E16] and recent screen highlights including net profit surging 338% year-over-year [E46]. Furthermore, domestic institutional investors have increased their conviction, raising their holdings by 2.13 percentage points to 6.59% in Sep 2026 [E33]. The broader macro environment provides strong backing as the Capital Goods sector sits firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.62 [E50]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -7.72 Cr alongside a cash conversion ratio of -2.35x for Mar 2026 [E26, E27].

The most critical vulnerability for Swastika Castal Ltd is a severe disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash flow of negative Rs 7.72 Cr and a free cash flow of negative Rs 12.95 Cr for March 2026 [E26, E28]. This cash drain results in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -2.35x against reported profit, signaling that earnings are not translating into liquid funds [E26]. Compounding this liquidity pressure, working capital requirements have deteriorated significantly, with working capital days nearly doubling from 74.8 days to 148 days [E42]. Furthermore, borrowings have ticked upward to Rs 11.67 Cr as of September 2026, forcing the company to rely on debt while cash drains persist [E30]. Operational stability is also a concern, as the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are both explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E24, E25]. Finally, despite reporting profits, the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield and is explicitly flagged for paying out no dividends to shareholders [E4, E41]. conceded: [E35]

Conceded: [E26, E28, E42]. While operating cash flow and free cash flow turned negative in March 2026 alongside expanding working capital days [E26, E28, E42], borrowings remain at a manageable Rs 11.67 Cr against a market capitalisation of ₹ 75.4 Cr and moderate leverage of 0.42x [E3, E29, E30]. The business is actively investing for future growth through a capital expenditure build-up, evidenced by capital work-in-progress rising 66.7% to Rs 0.55 Cr [E31]. This growth phase is supported by a strong macroeconomic backdrop with the Capital Goods sector in a clear tailwind [E48, E50]. Furthermore, despite operating margin volatility [E24, E25], long-term efficiency and profitability have expanded significantly, with TTM operating margins reaching 16% compared to 9% three years prior [E22], accompanied by robust return metrics like an 18% ROE and 19.6% ROCE [E12, E13]. Finally, the absence of dividend payouts [E4, E41] is typical for a high-growth company reinvesting its earnings to compound sales growth at 17% TTM [E15] and net profit growth at 338% YoY [E46].

Conceded: [E29, E30, E31]. While borrowings are modest at Rs 11.67 Cr against a ₹ 75.4 Cr market cap with 0.42x leverage [E3, E29, E30], and CWIP has risen [E31], this ongoing cash burn is severely undermining financial health rather than funding efficient expansion. Operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs -7.72 Cr and free cash flow to negative Rs -12.95 Cr for March 2026, creating a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -2.35x against reported profits [E26, E28]. This deterioration is directly visible in working capital, where days have doubled from 74.8 days to a bloated 148 days [E42]. Furthermore, dismissing the zero dividend yield [E4] as mere reinvestment ignores the official filing flag explicitly designating the lack of payouts as a negative for shareholders while profits fail to materialize as actual cash [E41]. The claimed margin and return expansions [E22, E12, E13] ring hollow when the underlying operating-margin trend is classified as inconsistent over both yearly and quarterly horizons [E24, E25].
